The maximum value of \(M\) is achieved by leveraging the bipartite nature of the \(8 \times 8\) grid graph, which consists of two sets: black cells where \(i + j\) is even and white cells where \(i + j\) is odd, each with 32 cells. Assign the larger half of the integers from 1 to 64 to the black cells (values 33 to 64) and the smaller half to the white cells (values 1 to 32). This ensures that for any adjacent pair (edge), the value in the black cell is greater than the value in the white cell, so \( |a_{i,j} - a_{k,l}| = a_{i,j} - a_{k,l} \) for any edge between a black cell and a white cell.

The expression for \(M\) simplifies to:
\[
M = \sum_{\text{black cells } u} \deg(u) a_u - \sum_{\text{white cells } v} \deg(v) b_v
\]
where \(\deg(u)\) is the degree of cell \(u\), \(a_u\) is the value assigned to black cell \(u\), and \(b_v\) is the value assigned to white cell \(v\).

The degrees of cells in the grid are distributed as follows for both sets:
- 2 cells have degree 2 (corner cells),
- 12 cells have degree 3 (edge cells, excluding corners),
- 18 cells have degree 4 (internal cells).

To maximize the expression:
1. For the black cells (assigned values 33 to 64), assign the largest values to the highest-degree cells:
   - Degree 4 cells (18 cells) get 47 to 64.
   - Degree 3 cells (12 cells) get 35 to 46.
   - Degree 2 cells (2 cells) get 33 and 34.
2. For the white cells (assigned values 1 to 32), to minimize \(\sum \deg(v) b_v\), assign the smallest values to the highest-degree cells:
   - Degree 4 cells (18 cells) get 1 to 18.
   - Degree 3 cells (12 cells) get 19 to 30.
   - Degree 2 cells (2 cells) get 31 and 32.

Compute \(\sum_{\text{black}} \deg(u) a_u\):
- Degree 2: \(2 \times 33 + 2 \times 34 = 134\)
- Degree 3: Values 35 to 46 sum to \(\frac{12}{2} \times (35 + 46) = 6 \times 81 = 486\), so \(3 \times 486 = 1458\)
- Degree 4: Values 47 to 64 sum to \(\frac{18}{2} \times (47 + 64) = 9 \times 111 = 999\), so \(4 \times 999 = 3996\)
- Total: \(134 + 1458 + 3996 = 5588\)

Compute \(\sum_{\text{white}} \deg(v) b_v\):
- Degree 4: Values 1 to 18 sum to \(\frac{18 \times 19}{2} = 171\), so \(4 \times 171 = 684\)
- Degree 3: Values 19 to 30 sum to \(\frac{12}{2} \times (19 + 30) = 6 \times 49 = 294\), so \(3 \times 294 = 882\)
- Degree 2: \(2 \times 31 + 2 \times 32 = 126\)
- Total: \(684 + 882 + 126 = 1692\)

Thus,
\[
M = 5588 - 1692 = 3896
\]

This assignment achieves the maximum possible \(M\), as it maximizes the sum of absolute differences given the bipartite constraints and optimal intra-set assignments. The remainder when 3896 is divided by 1000 is 896.
